name: SPACE
full_name: Student Project for an Axion Cavity Experiment
summary: A student-led microwave-cavity axion search in Hamburg that has published narrow-range searches in a strong magnetic field.
detection_principle: A tunable microwave cavity in a strong field enhances Galactic-axion conversion to microwave photons, seeking a narrowband excess in the noise spectrum.

status.label: Published experimental record; current overall operating status unverified
status.evidence: 2026 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: A new Limit for Axion Dark Matter with SPACE

collaboration.name: SPACE Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

results.summary: No significant signal; the best 95% CL axion–photon coupling sensitivity is 2.811×10⁻¹³ GeV⁻¹.

science_scope: Directly searches for Galactic-halo axions, axionlike particles or other ultralight dark matter. Limits depend on assumed local density, velocity distribution and coupling models; separate scanned mass intervals do not amount to exclusion of the entire range.
